title: AANTC - Algonquin Anishinabeg Nation Tribal Council language resources
publisher: Algonquin Anishinabeg Nation Tribal Council (AANTC / Conseil tribal de la nation algonquine anishinabeg, CTNAA)
edition: Tribal council language-resources website, English home page (en_CA), fetched 13 September 2026

extraction.command:
python3 -c 'import re,html,sys
p=sys.argv[1]
t=open(p,encoding="utf-8",errors="replace").read()
t=re.sub(r"(?is)\x3c(script|style|noscript)[^\x3e]*\x3e.*?\x3c/\1\x3e"," ",t)
t=re.sub(r"(?i)\x3cbr\s*/?\x3e","\n",t)
t=re.sub(r"(?i)\x3c/(p|div|li|h[1-6]|tr|section|article)\x3e","\n",t)
t=re.sub(r"(?s)\x3c[^\x3e]+\x3e"," ",t)
t=html.unescape(t)
t="\n".join(re.sub(r"[ \t\xa0]+"," ",l).strip() for l in t.split("\n"))
t=re.sub(r"\n{3,}","\n\n",t).strip()+"\n"
sys.stdout.write(t)' content/sources/aantc-home.html

knownStaleness.topic: The nation's own page spells it `Algonquin Anishinabeg`; the level spells it `Anishinabe Algonquin`
knownStaleness.problem: content/levels/ottawa.json's `nations` array holds the single value `Anishinabe Algonquin`, taken from the CROWN's wording in the level's `fact.source` - a Canada.ca news release datelined `Ottawa, unceded, unsurrendered territory of the Anishinabe Algonquin Nation`. This page, which is the tribal council's own, says `Welcome to the Algonquin Anishinabeg Nation Tribal Council language resources website` and `various Algonquin dialects`. The string `Anishinabe Algonquin` does not occur on it in that order; `Anishinabe` occurs only as the first nine letters of `Anishinabeg`. So the `nationSource` for this level does not literally contain the name the level records, and the two orderings come from two different authorities - the nation's own, and the Crown's.
knownStaleness.action: do not edit either string to make a check pass. Which order this project ships is a question about whose name it is, and per docs/content-review.md 3.1 and 9.3 the answer runs toward the nation's own page rather than the news release. Route it; a verifier may not settle it by normalising, and an author may not settle it by preferring the Crown's word order because it is the one already written down.

knownStaleness.topic: A language-resources site, not a territory page
knownStaleness.problem: This is the tribal council's Anishinabemowin teaching site: colouring books, story books, picture dictionaries and curriculum resources for Barriere Lake, Kitcisakik, Kitigan Zibi, Lac Simon, Long Point, Pikogan, Timiskaming, Wahgoshig and Abitibiwinni. The words `territory`, `Ottawa` and `unceded` appear nowhere on it. It supports that the Algonquin Anishinabeg Nation Tribal Council exists, publishes in its own language, and names those communities. It supports nothing about where Ottawa stands.
knownStaleness.action: the Ottawa territorial claim rests entirely on cirnac-algonquin-parliamentary-precinct, a Crown source. docs/content-review.md 10.2 asks for the nation's own material where one exists, and this cache is evidence that for this level the nation's own material - at this URL - does not carry the fact. Report that rather than treating the pairing as settled.

knownStaleness.topic: Part of the page is behind a login
knownStaleness.problem: The navigation carries `Account`, `Register`, `Login`, `Logout`, `Members` and `Password Reset`, and the page says in its own words: `Some resources are restricted on this site. To gain access, please contact: anishinabemowin@aantc-ctnaa.ca`. What is cached here is the anonymous view. There is material on this site that this project fetched nothing of, and which it has no standing to request.
knownStaleness.action: do not attempt to reach the restricted material. Record the anonymous view as the anonymous view, and if a claim ever needs what is behind the login, the answer is that the claim cannot be made.

grainNote: One web page and two headings. Three flags: a name spelled two ways by two authorities, a source that does not carry the fact the level pairs it with, and a part of the site nobody here may read. The first two are findings about content/levels/ottawa.json rather than about this document, and they are here because this is the file the next reader will open.
